epithet: You are the ones in need of Allah
lede: It opens with the angels and their wings, and with a mercy no one can hold back once He has released it. Then it tells mankind its true position — the poor before the Rich — and says who, among all His servants, really fears Him: those who know.

names.name: Fāṭir
names.note: From its first ayah: Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth. Ibn ʿAbbās said he did not understand the word until two Bedouin came to him disputing over a well, and one of them said, “Anā faṭartuhā” — it was I who first dug it.

names.name: al-Malāʾikah
names.note: A name Ibn al-Jawzī records, from the same ayah: “who made the angels messengers, with wings, two and three and four.”

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. The traditional order places it forty-third.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ فاطِرٍ وَتُسَمّى سُورَةَ المَلائِكَةِ، وهي مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ
قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: ما كُنْتُ أدْرِي ما فاطِرُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ حَتّى اخْتَصَمَ أعْرابِيّانِ في بِئْرٍ، فَقالَ أحَدُهُما: أنا فَطَرْتُها، أيِ: ابْتَدَأتُها

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في ”الدَّلائِلِ“ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةُ ”فاطِرٍ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: No occasion is reported for it. It is the last of the five surahs that open with “Praise be to Allah”, and it reads as one sustained act of drawing attention: look at what you have been given, and from whom.

It is addressed, more than most, to mankind as such — “O mankind” comes three times. The first: remember Allah’s favour upon you; is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? The second: the promise of Allah is true, so do not let this life deceive you. And the third states the relation in a sentence: “O mankind, it is you who are the poor, in need of Allah; and Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy.”

To the Prophet ﷺ, who was being called a liar, it says twice that this is how messengers have always been received, and tells him not to wear himself out with grief over those whose evil has been made to look good to them. “You cannot make those in the graves hear. You are only a warner.”

Then comes a passage that the scholars of every age have returned to. Rain falls, and the fruit it brings out is of every colour; the mountains are streaked white and red and deep black; people, beasts and cattle differ in their colours likewise. “Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.” And of those to whom the Book was given as an inheritance it distinguishes three: the one who wrongs himself, the one who keeps a middle course, and the one who is foremost in good deeds, by Allah’s leave. All three are of those He chose.
aim: To display the scenes of Allah’s power and His originality in creation, and what moves a person to revere Him, fear Him, believe in Him and remember His favours.
themes: Knowledge and the fear of Allah
The three inheritors of the Book

outline.title: The Originator, and His mercy
outline.summary: Praise be to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers with wings — two, three and four; He adds to creation as He wills. Whatever mercy Allah opens to people, none can withhold it; and what He withholds, none can release. O mankind, remember Allah’s favour upon you. If they deny you, messengers before you were denied. Satan is an enemy to you, so treat him as an enemy. Do not let your soul waste away in grief over them.

outline.title: Signs of His power
outline.summary: It is Allah who sends the winds that raise the clouds, and We drive them to a dead land and revive it: such is the resurrection. Whoever desires honour — all honour belongs to Allah. To Him the good word ascends, and the righteous deed raises it. The two seas are not alike: one sweet, one bitter, and from each you eat fresh meat. Those you call on besides Him do not own so much as the skin of a date-stone.

outline.title: The poor, and the Rich
outline.summary: O mankind, you are the poor in need of Allah, and Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy. If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor darkness and light, nor shade and heat, nor the living and the dead. You are only a warner; and there is no nation but a warner has passed among it.

outline.title: Those who know, and those given the Book
outline.summary: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring out by it fruits of differing colours; and in the mountains are streaks white and red, and raven-black; and people, beasts and cattle likewise of differing colours? Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah (35:28). Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those of Our servants whom We chose: among them one who wrongs himself, one who is moderate, and one who is foremost in good deeds. They will enter Gardens of Eden, and say: “Praise be to Allah, who has removed sorrow from us.”

outline.title: The disbelievers’ plea
outline.summary: For those who disbelieve is the fire of Hell. They will cry out in it: “Our Lord, bring us out; we will do right, not what we used to do.” — “Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed? And the warner came to you.” Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease; and if they were to cease, no one could hold them after Him.

outline.title: The oath they broke
outline.summary: They swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them they would be better guided than any nation. But when a warner came, it increased them only in aversion. The evil plot encloses none but its authors. If Allah were to take people to task for what they have earned, He would not leave a creature on the face of the earth; but He defers them to an appointed term.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s address to every human being, and the truth on which worship rests: the need is all on one side.

before: Sabaʾ opened with praise and told of blessings met with thanks and with ingratitude. Fāṭir opens with praise again, and bids all mankind remember the favour.
after: Fāṭir ends with a people who swore that if a warner came to them they would follow him. Yā-Sīn opens by swearing that he has come: “You are indeed one of the messengers.”
